decision_clause: Ruled out: "keep the wildcard census and rely on the focused-lane guard" — because "the guard catches deletion only, and the review demonstrated growth passing 230/230 with an unreviewed product file present". Scope: packages/schema/src/capability.ts, packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs; lifecycle active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so no census, guard, or contract shape was altered by this task. In that tree the file census is not wildcard-based and is not deletion-only. tests/planning-contract.test.mjs:34-35 pin the validator's output against a literal that enumerates all 64 ticket-owned code paths together with exact counts (control_plane_code_files=17, ticket_owned_code_files=64, product_code_files=0, product_code_paths=none), so an added source file changes the emitted list and count and fails the assertion. tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs performs an exhaustive recursive filesystem walk of packages/adapters/suites/fixtures/conformance and asserts deepEqual against a ticket-derived allowlist (line ~397), and its 'skeleton-source-requires-an-owning-ticket' test re-runs scripts/validate-planning.mjs and asserts the reported census equals the independently re-derived owned set. The growth direction is exercised positively: 'doctor-fixture-admission-honours-the-declared-file-predicate' copies the repository, writes a NEW undeclared file into it, and asserts the census run fails and names that file. scripts/validate-planning.mjs:861-868 classifies any source file that is neither control-plane-allowlisted nor ticket-claimed as product code and errors out, i.e. it fails closed on addition, not only on removal. Separately and independently of the decision question: validateCapabilityMatrix in packages/schema/src/capability.ts still returns the flat shape { ok: boolean; errors; rows: CapabilityRow[]; required_event_groups; coverage } (type at lines 49-55, returns at 268, 271, 432), and packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts contains no discriminated-union or type-level assertions — so the requested contract change was not made at all.
rationale: The finished tree contains no change whatsoever relative to the base tree, so it cannot have newly introduced the ruled-out arrangement. Reading the tree directly confirms the same conclusion on the merits: the in-scope census files implement an exhaustive-walk plus exact-enumeration census that fails closed when a file is added, with a dedicated test that stages an undeclared new file and requires the census to reject it by name — the precise failure mode ('the guard catches deletion only... growth passing with an unreviewed product file present') that the decision cited as its reason. No wildcard/glob-discovery census stands in for that enumeration in packages/schema, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, or tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs. The label holds under the opposite reading of the decision text as well: if one instead read the ruled-out thing as replacing the wildcard census, an unchanged tree replaces nothing either. I note for completeness, though it does not bear on the decision, that the task itself (the ok:true/ok:false discriminated result contract and its added coverage) is unimplemented in this tree; that is a delivery gap, not a violation of the recorded decision.
